title: Walsall to Stourbridge Corridor Options Assessment Report
description:
In line with the strategic direction of the Local Transport Plan, Transport for West Midlands (TfWM) is working on developing mass rapid transit solutions as part of an integrated public transport network in the West Midlands.  The term Mass Rapid Transit is used as a mode agnostic term covering large capacity, fixed route, timetabled public transport solutions encompassing rail, light rail, bus rapid transit etc.   

This is done to try and prevent a focus on a specific solution or output when developing schemes.  As part of the development, focus will be placed on specific outcomes and impacts.  As a result, the development work will be problem-led and evidence based to ensure an objective assessment of the right intervention, in the right place at the right time. 

In conjunction with Walsall Metropolitan Borough Council (WMBC), Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council (SMBC) and Dudley Borough Council (DBC), TfWM is issuing this brief to appoint a suitable consultant to undertake the development of an Options Assessment for the Walsall to Stourbridge Corridor.

description:

      what future Museum would support the wider regeneration of the Borough? 
      where would the future Museum be best located?  
      
      Capturing the momentum, both local through the Walsall Heritage Strategy (2021-2026) and regionally following the cultural successful Birmingham Commonwealth Games 2022, this is an exciting opportunity to re-imagine Walsall's Museum offer, interrogating the existing model and proposing a fresh vision, ethos, and overall approach for a unique and innovative space in Walsall.

title: WP4008 - Walsall Creative Commissions - AWARD
description:
The Council wishes to procure a high-quality provider to deliver 'Walsall Imagining Spaces', a creative commissioning programme funded by The Commonwealth Games Legacy Enhancement Fund (CWGLEF) Cultural Pillar. 
      
      Walsall Imagining Spaces aims to support exciting projects working with new and underrepresented communities and parts of the borough that might not always receive investment for culture. The programme is aimed at enhancing opportunities to experience and participate in cultural and creative arts and seeks creative organisations to come forward with ideas for imaginative projects that will reach out and into Walsall's diverse communities. 
      
      Delivery of cultural programming will actively seek to engage communities through established, integrated networks, inc. Walsall Cultural Compact, to champion the borough's broad cultural sector. The approach is to commission a cultural sector partner resourcing three key strands of delivery, themed around the aspirational imagining of our shared public spaces to attract residents and visitors to urban centres.  
      
      Firstly, prime locations will be allocated for temporary public art commissions, as a proven concept via the Council endorsed National Highways M6 Junction 10 Art Competition. Further success of recent campaigns including the Knife Angel, Picturing High Streets, Walsall Canal Street, amongst others, provides evidence for both demand and impact of temporary installations in increasing footfall, improving sense of place and presenting our collective ambition for the future of Walsall. Evaluation will capture learning informing future public art approaches.  
      
      Secondly, cultural events will be funded with a focus on enhancing the town centre market offer and third, broader cultural activities will be funded through a capacity building and competitive grants programme, capitalising on the well-networked third sector, and wider independent practitioners, located across the Borough. Walsall's VCS and cultural sector is distinct in the role of broader third sector organisations in delivering community activity alongside sector-specific projects, such arts and culture. Existing engagement through the Walsall Heritage Strategy and wider support organisations, provide the basis for a comprehensive programme of live commissions to support experiential engagement with town centre and high street locations.

title: WP4110 - Evaluation Consultancy as part of Our Heritage: Walsall Community Heritage Fund Programme  - AWARD
description:
Walsall Council is seeking a high-quality provider to undertake an expert evaluation of: Our Heritage: Walsall Community Heritage Fund (1st April 2025 - 30th September 2028).  
      
      Supported by the National Lottery Heritage Fund in 2025 Walsall Council received a £249,840 grant to deliver the Our Heritage Programme. Central to the project is the upscale of crowdfunding and engagement programmes that will enable heritage organisations to access funding, forge partnerships/supporter networks, and build resilience. 15-20 groups over 4 cohorts are expected to benefit, promoting innovation to champion Walsall's underrepresented heritage. 12 participatory grant making opportunities will be available to further enhance community voice in decision-making.
      
      Alongside this, the programme includes refreshment of the Heritage Action Plan, to guide discussions, set direction and identify sector needs over a 5-year period and beyond. The aim of the first, 2021-2026, strategy was to place heritage at the heart of Walsall's future, protecting what exists whilst nurturing sustainability and identifying opportunities to unlock its full value.
      
      The project vision is to ensure that heritage is better managed through a new Plan, integrated into Walsall's overall vision and transformation, meeting the needs of a diverse local population who are proud to live, work and visit Walsall.

title: WP3968 - One Palfrey Big Local Parks and Play - AWARD
description:
Project Overview 
      Walsall Council is looking to appoint a single competent contractor to complete parks projects under the 'One Palfrey Big Local Parks and Play' scheme. 
      
      One Palfrey Big Local is a resident led programme supported by a Local Trusted Organisation (Walsall Council for the parks and play project) and a Big Local Rep. The Partnership consists of 12 residents who live in the OPBL area.
      
      One Palfrey Big Local partnership guides the Big Local making decisions about funding. To achieve OPBL's vision, residents chose four priorities that are based on the changes they most want to see:
      
      o A cleaner and safer Palfrey neighbourhood
      o Healthier residents with a sense of community & wellbeing
      o Better access to jobs, training and lifelong learning
      o Improved community activities and services for all.
      
      As part of these priorities and local consultation the OPBL decided to look at a park and play improvement programme for 3 local sites.
      
      The scheme has been consulted on at all stages with local communities through OPBL  which has resulted in the following sites being selected for the works summarised.
      
      1. Palfrey Park - Dale Street, Palfrey, Walsall West Midlands WS1 4AN. 
      Play Area Improvements / North and South park landscaping / Park Furniture Improvement.
      
      2. Bescot Crescent Play Area, Bescot Crescent, Walsall West Midlands WS1 4DH 
      Play Area Improvements / Small scale planting / Park Furniture Improvement.
      
      3. Arena Park - aka known as Rutter Street Play Area), Rutter Street, Walsall, West Midlands. WS1 4HN
      Improvements / Park landscaping / Park Furniture Improvement / Improvements to MUGA (Multi Use Games Area).
      
      Procurement 
      
      The route to market being used is a mini competition under the Pagabo Dynamic Purchasing System for Small Works. The framework fee applicable to is 1.5% which is charged monthly. 
      
      The works are to be procured via a single stage tender process.  
      
      Budget
      The project is funded by One Palfrey Big Local, with a maximum budget of ?458,300 
      
      If the costs come in above the budget the Council reserves the right to omit certain items listed within the commercial workbooks or opt to add in later should additional funding be available etc. 
      
      During the tender period bidders will be given the opportunity to provide costs for alternative products to those specified as a cost saving initiative.  
      
      The timescale for this project are currently works to be complete and money spent by end of March 2025.  However following contractors feedback from the EOI, the Council are in the process of formally requesting an extension until 4th August 2025.

title: WP4068 - Ryecroft Community Hub  - AWARD
description:
Walsall Council is looking to appoint a single competent contractor to deliver Ryecroft Community Hub's Energy Improvements. 
      
      The Ryecroft Community Hub project aims to improve the energy efficiency of the building. Works involve upgrades to the building fabric, including replacing windows with new triple glazed units, installing a new external wall insulation system, and installing a new insulated suspended ceiling. In addition to these passive measures, the project will also include the installation of a new roof mounted photovoltaic panel system, electric vehicle charging points, and replacement of internal lighting with new LED fittings.
      
      Project Location: Ryecroft Community Hub, 40 New Forest Road, Walsall WS3 1TR
      
      Designs provided within this tender are up to RIBA Stage 4. 
      
      The route to market being used is a mini competition under the Pagabo Decarbonisation Solutions - AVP-HCC-1001. The framework fee applicable to contractors is 0.25% which is charge monthly. 
      
      The works are to be procured as part of a single stage process.

      This project is solely funded by the 'Bloxwich Town Deal Programme' which is externally funded by Government as part of its previous Levelling Up Programme. 
      
      Under the funding terms, all works must be completed and grant funding spent before the imposed deadline of the 31 March 2026

title: WP3901a - Creative Industries Enterprise Centre - AWARD
description:
The Council is looking for one contractor for the Internal and External refurbishment works of the Guildhall to create a new Creative Industries Enterprise Centre (CIEC) using a 2 stage procurement process via  a mini competition under the Constructing West Midlands (CWM) Lot 1.
      
      Walsall Council has been successful in securing funding from Central Government through their Town Deal and Cultural Development Funds to acquire and re-purpose the derelict Grade 2 listed former Guildhall, the former Police Station and 32/34 Goodall Street buildings to be used as a Creative Industries Enterprise Centre (CIEC).
      
      The CIEC will provide an opportunity to those with creative skills and industry knowledge seeking an innovative and alternative avenue from which to find employment. It will form part of a wider town ecosystem designed to support creative industries success, as well as supporting the future health and vitality of the town centre.
      
      The new larger premise in the town centre, presents a unique opportunity to implement many of the current plans and activities and identified future opportunities, such as an enhanced makerspace, café/informal meeting space, tap room, artisan workspace, meeting rooms, and craft retail outlets. The project aims to secure one of three historical properties fronting the High Street in the St Matthews Quarter, which are currently neglected and vacant and bring them back into economic use bringing vitality and life back into this area.
      
      The CIEC will be run by the Social Enterprise Organisation - Urban Hax who successfully developed multi-purpose "makers space" for a number of startup businesses with Walsall and provide shared work-shop type space for a range of small craft industries. The makerspace will intend to give the public access to tools and equipment that are not commercially available. Through talks, classes, workshops, collaborative projects, and other activities, to encourage research, knowledge exchange, learning, and mentoring in safe, clean, workspaces for projects related to art, science, and technology. The project will provide creative individuals the space and facilities to run their own business and support them as their businesses grow
      
      Works overview
      Following early pre-market engagement with contractors' designs have been developed to RIBA 4 (with exclusion of contractor design portions) and enabling stripping out works are currently being undertaken and will have completed prior to the contract start of the project.
      
      Works will comprise the external and internal refurbishment. External repairs will be undertaken to the building elevations. Internally the building will be reconfigured to provide a flexible makerspace.

title: WP4057b Shepwell School Modular Teaching Block Installation
description:
This contract is for the provision of constructing of a new teaching block with associated groundworks at the rear of the site of the existing Shepwell School to accommodate an additional 50 special educational needs (SEN) pupils together with additional playground facilities.

The Shepwell School located on Bilston Lane in the town of Willenhall in Walsall was built in the 1970s as an Adult Education Centre, now operates as a Short Stay School and Specialist Autism Resource Base. It accommodates pupils aged 11-16 with social, emotional, and complex educational needs. The project is to address a shortfall in SEND school places by increasing capacity from 84 to 134 pupils through the addition of a new two-storey teaching block. The modular design will minimise construction disruption and improve site safety, sustainability, and accessibility.

The works required comprise a new modular building with associated pathway external works, a new canopy to connect to the existing school with adaptation of the existing canopy walkways. Facilities should be aligned with Building Bulletin 104 for SEND pupils. A piled foundation solution has been designed and pumped drainage will be required to suit existing levels.

A Phase II Site Investigation has been undertaken during w/c 17/02/2025. An interim report will be made available at the earliest opportunity during the tender period.

The site will remain a live environment during the works and will remain in use for its duration. The Contractor is to ensure that the working areas are separated from the school area and allow for fencing/hoarding as necessary. There should be no interaction between unauthorised Contractor's staff and staff and pupils of the school.

Walsall Council is looking to appoint a single competent contractor on the CWM Framework (Lot 1) to extend the current provision within the school to provide additional classrooms to facilitate non ambulant pupils.  
      
      Oakwood School is a specialist provision for children aged 3 - 14 years with complex educational needs.  The school is commissioned for 238 places (September 2024).
      
      The project involves the demolition of the existing outdoor classroom structure to make way for a new single-storey extension. Accessibility is prioritised with the inclusion of wider than standard doorsets and two new external access ramps designed to comply with current standards.

Externally, hard landscaping will be reinstated around the new extension to match the existing finishes.
      
      The site will remain a live environment during the works and will remain in use. 
      
      The works must be completed by 22 August 2025 to ensure the provision is in place for the September 2025 term.

title: WP3846 - York's Bridge (Construction) - AWARD
description:
Walsall Council is looking for a suitably qualified contractor to complete the construction of a new replacement York's Bridge on Norton Road, Pelsall, which spans the Wyrley and Essington Canal by the Fingerpost public house. 
      
      Background of the existing York's Bridge
      The existing historic York's Bridge dates back to the mid 1800's.  Its brick arch construction, poor alignments and lack of footways make it unsuitable for modern traffic and unsafe for pedestrians and cyclists.  The bridge structure has suffered over recent decades and the bridge is currently the subject of a 10 tonne weight limit.  If nothing is done the bridge will continue to weaken to the point where closure to all road traffic might have to be considered.
      The Council has a statutory duty to maintain the safe and efficient operation of the public highway for use by a range of vehicles and is obliged to look at a range of options, including the strengthening of bridges which it does not own, (the existing bridge is owned by the Canal & River Trust), and the construction of new bridges.
      Several options for addressing the problems at York's Bridge have been considered, including strengthening of the existing bridge.  It has been concluded that only the construction of a new bridge can address all of the issues, whilst retaining the existing historic York's Bridge 
      
      The new York's Bridge
      The construction of a new bridge aims to create a healthier and safer environment for people to walk and cycle and traffic moving through the area.  The new bridge will be constructed to the east side of the existing bridge and to realign Norton Road to the east. The bridge is 40m long and will carry two-way traffic on a 7.3m wide carriageway with a 2m wide footway on the west side. There is 2m minimum headroom between the bridge and towpath and 3.1m minimum between the bridge and canal. A small amount (2,465m2) of common land is required in order to construct the new bridge which is less than 0.01% of the total common area.
